label: A. J. Ayer, Language Ch: Ayer reports that some positivists have proposed conclusive verifiability…
locator: ch. I, p. 18, "if we adopt conclusive verifiability as our criterion of significance, as some positivists have proposed"
interpretation: Ayer's report, with footnote 6 citing Schlick's 1931 paper on causality. This is the textual basis for reading V1 as conclusive verification; it attributes the view to Schlick 1931 through Ayer, not to Schlick's 1936 paper.
attribution: The passage states that some positivists have proposed conclusive verifiability as the criterion of significance, citing Schlick 1931 in a footnote, which is the premise.
